classification.difficultyReason: The height part scaffolds the triangle area, but students must independently identify three 60-degree sectors and account for their shared triangle, subtracting its area twice. This connects Pythagoras, sector geometry and overlapping areas.

content.prompt: A company logo consists of an equilateral triangle with an arc of a circle drawn on each side using the opposite vertex as centre. If the length of each side of the equilateral triangle is 6 cm, find:

spec.sourceRegion: Chapter 16 review, question 3, logo to the right
spec.description: Unshaded equilateral triangle with upper vertex and horizontal base. Three outward circular arcs join its vertices; each arc is centred at the opposite vertex. All three straight triangle sides remain visible. Decorative source blue is replaced by house black.
spec.mathematics: Each triangle side and each arc radius is 6 cm. Each arc subtends 60 degrees at its centre. No dimensions or calculated quantities are printed in the figure.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied triangle and outer arcs are visible.

children.label: a
children.prompt: the height of the triangle (giving an exact answer)

answer.worked:
The perpendicular height bisects the 6 cm base.
$$\begin{align*}h^2&=6^2-3^2\\h^2&=27\\h&=3\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: the area of the logo, correct to 2 decimal places

answer.short:
$25.37\text{ cm}^2$

Add the three $60^\circ$ sectors and subtract twice the triangle's area.
answer.worked:
Each sector has radius 6 cm and angle $60^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{triangle}}&=\frac12\times6\times3\sqrt3\\A_{\text{triangle}}&=9\sqrt3\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{sector}}&=\frac{60}{360}\times\pi\times6^2\\A_{\text{sector}}&=6\pi\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
The logo consists of the triangle and three circular segments. Adding the three sectors counts the triangle three times, so subtract its area twice.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{logo}}&=3(6\pi)-2(9\sqrt3)\\A_{\text{logo}}&=18\pi-18\sqrt3\\A_{\text{logo}}&\approx25.37\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
